question.value: Investigate the consistency of different star formation rate tracers, dust attenuation corrections, and star formation histories in 12 massive Lyman-break galaxies at z = 6.5-7.7 using JWST NIRSpec IFU and ALMA observations.

evidence.quote: To address this problem, we investigate the SFRs of 12 massive ($9~<~\log$($M_{\star}$/${\rm M}_{\odot}$) $<~10$) Lyman-break galaxies at $z=6.5-7.7$, drawn from the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) Reionization Era Bright Emission Line Survey (REBELS) program.
We compare SFRs derived from the rest-UV, H$\alpha$, and far-infrared emission, and from spectral energy distribution (SED) fits.
ALMA Band 6 or Band 7 observations of these sources were obtained as part of the Cycle 7 REBELS ALMA large program (PID: 2019.1.01634.L, P.I. Bouwens).
Improved constraints on the remaining sources will soon be possible thanks to recent Band 8 observations (PID: 2024.1.00406.S, P.I. Algera).

findings_qualitative.value: Differential dust attenuation remains important at z~7, with an average stellar-to-nebular colour excess ratio of f = 0.50 +/- 0.08, showing no clear evolution with redshift compared to local galaxies.

evidence.quote: We find an average stellar-to-nebular attenuation ratio of $f = E(B-V)_{\text{stellar}}/E(B-V)_{\text{gas}} = 0.50 \pm 0.08$, indicating that differential attenuation remains significant in massive, $z\simeq7$ galaxies.

findings_qualitative.value: Between 56% and 78% of star formation in the massive REBELS-IFU galaxies is dust-obscured, and the IRX-beta relation implies a dust attenuation curve intermediate between Calzetti and SMC.

evidence.quote: The average attenuation curve inferred from the ${\rm IRX}$–$\beta$ relation lies between the Calzetti-like and SMC relations, consistent with the attenuation curves derived directly from the NIRSpec rest-UV/optical spectra in (cite: Fisher2025).

findings_qualitative.value: Steeply rising SFHs cause standard rest-UV+FIR SFR calibrations (which assume constant SFHs over 100 Myr) to trace a shorter ~20 Myr timescale and overestimate the 100 Myr average SFR by a factor of ~2.7.

evidence.quote: These discrepancies can be explained with rising SFHs, which causes SFR$_{\text{UV+IR}}$ (calculated using the fiducial luminosity-to-SFR conversion factors that are derived assuming a constant SFH) to match the SFR averaged over a timescale of $\sim20$ Myr, not the assumed $100$ Myrs.

findings_qualitative.value: The Halpha-to-UV luminosity ratio is an unreliable diagnostic of bursty star formation in galaxies with rising SFHs.

evidence.quote: This suggests the H$\alpha$-to-UV luminosity ratio is not a reliable indicator of bursty SFHs, even with robust dust attenuation corrections.

claims.hypothesis: Does the stellar-to-nebular dust attenuation ratio evolve toward unity at z ~ 7, or does differential dust attenuation remain similar to local star-forming galaxies?

claims.result: A linear fit yields f = E(B-V)_stellar / E(B-V)_gas = 0.50 +/- 0.08, though individual galaxies scatter between 0.1 and 1.

claims.finding: Steeply rising SFHs cause standard rest-UV conversion factors to overestimate the 100 Myr average SFR by nearly a factor of 3.

evidence.loc: Tracer timescales and rising SFHs cause SFR discrepancies
evidence.quote: We find comparable factors in the REBELS-IFU sample, with SFR$_{\text{UV+IR}}$ and SFR$_{\text{UV, intrinsic SED}}$ exceeding SFR$_{\text{100 Myr}}$ by median factors of 2.3 and 2.7, respectively.

Comparing these to the values in Table [\[tab:SFREqns\]](#tab:SFREqns) that are derived assuming constant SFHs, we see that $\kappa_{\text{H}\alpha}$ remains approximately consistent, but there is a large systematic shift in $\kappa_{\text{UV}}$ by a factor of $\simeq2.7$ ($>0.4$ dex).

claims.hypothesis: Is the Halpha-to-UV luminosity ratio a reliable diagnostic of bursty star formation in z ~ 7 galaxies with rising SFHs?
claims.experiment: Compare dust-corrected log(L_Halpha / nu L_nu,1600) against SED-derived log(SFR_10Myr / SFR_100Myr) for the REBELS-IFU sample and BAGPIPES rising-SFH models.
claims.result: All REBELS-IFU galaxies have log(SFR_10Myr / SFR_100Myr) > 0.2 (bursty), yet all but one have L_Halpha / nu L_nu,1600 consistent within 1-sigma with the constant-SFH equilibrium value.
claims.finding: The Halpha-to-UV ratio is an unreliable indicator of bursty star formation because rising SFHs shift the effective timescale of the UV continuum toward that of Halpha.

evidence.quote: Despite all the REBELS-IFU galaxies having SFR$_{10~\text{Myr}}$/SFR$_{100~\text{Myr}}>1$, indicative of bursty SFHs, the observed H$\alpha$-to-UV luminosity ratios for all but one of the galaxies remain consistent (within $1\sigma$) with the non-bursty value.
This suggests the H$\alpha$-to-UV luminosity ratio is not a reliable indicator of bursty SFHs, even with robust dust attenuation corrections.

why_this_data.value: REBELS-IFU is the only sample of massive (M_* > 10^9 M_sun) galaxies at z > 6 that combines rest-UV/optical JWST NIRSpec IFU spectroscopy with rest-FIR ALMA observations, enabling direct comparison of unobscured and obscured SFR tracers.

evidence.quote: REBELS-IFU provides a unique dataset for comparing SFR tracers at $z\simeq7$ since multi-wavelength observations extending from the rest-frame UV/optical (*JWST* NIRSpec spectroscopy) to the rest-frame FIR (ALMA) are available (cite: Bouwens2022).

This is the only sample of massive ($M_{\star}$ $>10^{9}$ ${\rm M}_{\odot}$) galaxies at $z>6$ that has this wealth of SFR tracers, providing a unique opportunity to investigate the consistency between different methods and shed light on the SFHs of these sources.

why_this_method.value: Combining direct Balmer decrement nebular corrections, flexible-attenuation-curve SED fitting, and ALMA FIR measurements reduces the reliance on untested local calibration assumptions.

evidence.quote: From the NIRSpec spectra, we have measurements of key physical properties of these galaxies, including stellar mass (Stefanon et al. in prep.), dust attenuation curves (cite: Fisher2025), and gas-phase metallicities (cite: Rowland2025), allowing us to build up a comprehensive picture of these galaxies and reduce the number of assumptions required.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Inferring nebular attenuation from stellar continuum attenuation using a fixed average f ratio for the four z > 7 galaxies without Halpha coverage was rejected due to the large galaxy-to-galaxy scatter in f (0.1 to 1).

evidence.loc: Differential dust attenuation is still important at $\mathbf{z\simeq7}$
evidence.quote: While our average relation is consistent with the commonly assumed $f=0.44$ factor, we caution that for individual galaxies, inferring the nebular attenuation from the continuum attenuation using this linear relation is unreliable since $f$ ranges between $0.1$ and $1$ in our sample (with a standard deviation of $0.27$).

evidence.loc: Differential dust attenuation is still important at $\mathbf{z\simeq7}$
evidence.quote: This justifies our decision to exclude from our analysis the SFR$_{\text{H}\alpha}$ values for galaxies in the REBELS-IFU sample for which we cannot measure the Balmer decrement.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Using the multi-band ALMA L_IR from Algera et al. (2023) for REBELS-12 was rejected because it is undetected in Band 8, leaving the FIR SED poorly constrained.

evidence.loc: Deriving SFRs from the rest-UV, H$\alpha$, and FIR luminosities
evidence.quote: We do not use the $L_{\rm IR}$ derived by (cite: Algera2023) for REBELS-12 since it is undetected in the Band 8 data and thus, the constraints on the FIR SED are poor.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: SED fits with a constant SFH over >= 100 Myr were rejected because they poorly fit the rest-optical continuum and lack of a Balmer break.

evidence.quote: SED fits with a constant SFH constrained to have a minimum timescale of at least $100$ Myr fit the spectra poorly.

limitations_admitted.value: For the four galaxies at z > 7, Halpha is redshifted out of the NIRSpec coverage and Hgamma is blended in the R~100 prism spectra, preventing direct Balmer decrement measurements and nebular attenuation curve constraints.

evidence.loc: Correcting SFRs with dust attenuation curves
evidence.quote: For the four REBELS-IFU galaxies at $z>7$ (REBELS-12, REBELS-14, REBELS-18, and REBELS-25), H$\alpha$ is redshifted beyond the wavelength range of NIRSpec.

evidence.loc: Differential dust attenuation is still important at $\mathbf{z\simeq7}$
evidence.quote: Unfortunately, we are unable to place strong constraints on the nebular attenuation curve for our galaxies by comparing multiple Balmer line ratios, since in our PRISM spectra H$\gamma$ is blended with other emission lines and the signal-to-noise (S/N) ratios of higher-order Balmer emission lines are too low.

limitations_admitted.value: For most of the sample, L_IR relies on a single ALMA band detection assuming a fixed dust temperature T_d = 46 K and emissivity beta_d = 2.0.

evidence.quote: We note the usual caveats of assuming a fixed dust temperature, $T_{\rm d}$, when calculating $L_{\rm IR}$.
For most of our sample, only a single ALMA band detection is available to constrain the modified blackbody SED fit to the rest-frame FIR continuum

limitations_admitted.value: The REBELS-IFU sample is biased toward higher SFRs due to rest-UV bright selection (M_UV < -21) and bright [CII] 158 um selection.

evidence.quote: The dashed horizontal line shows the approximate SFR threshold of the REBELS survey introduced by the rest-UV bright selection (${M_{\rm UV}}$$\lesssim-21.5$) and the dust continuum sensitivity limits of the ALMA observations.
The 12 REBELS-IFU sources have some of the brightest $158~\mu$m detections from the REBELS survey, further biasing this subsample to higher SFRs (cite: DeLooze2014).

limitations_admitted.value: Spatial offsets between rest-UV and FIR emitting regions and outshining in integrated spectra could affect energy balance assumptions and stellar mass estimates.

evidence.loc: Consistency between SFRs derived from the rest-UV
evidence.quote: Another effect we must consider that could affect the recovery of the total SFRs is the impact of dust-star geometry.
We note that stellar masses derived from integrated spectra can be underestimated compared to pixel-based estimates due to outshining (cite: Gimenez-Artega2024).

referee_caveats_inferred: The analysis relies heavily on upstream results from companion papers (Stefanon et al. in prep., Fisher et al. 2025, Rowland et al. 2025, Bowler et al. 2023) rather than reducing raw ALMA or JWST data in this work.
Single-band ALMA continuum measurements for 10/12 sources require assuming a fixed dust temperature (T_d = 46 K), which introduces ~0.4 dex systematic uncertainty per 10 K shift in L_IR.

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: <1 GB for catalog tables and 1D integrated spectra (~50-200 GB if starting from raw archival ALMA visibilities and JWST cubes)
reproducibility.score_reason: The equations, conversion factors, and derived properties per galaxy (Tables 1 and 3) are clearly tabulated, making downstream algebraic checks easy, but the underlying 1D NIRSpec spectra, individual attenuation curves, and SFH posteriors are inherited from companion papers (including one in prep.) and only available upon request.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: This paper performs downstream multi-wavelength synthesis and SED/SFR analysis using published ALMA luminosities from Bowler et al. (2023) and Algera et al. (2023, 2024) rather than direct ALMA visibility or image analysis, and key JWST data reduction details reside in an unpublished companion paper (Stefanon et al. in prep.).
